paragraphs.text: Lorwyn-Shadowmoor is a remote Celtic -inspired plane with two aspects. While Lorwyn represents day, Shadowmoor is night. Previously, Lorwyn and Shadowmoor interchanged cyclically every 300 years, an unnatural event triggered by the Great Aurora . Following Oona 's defeat, both aspects of the plane simultaneously exist, bleeding into each other.

Lorwyn-Shadowmoor does not stand out in the Blind Eternities ; it resides in a region of dream and aether that obscures it from most planeswalkers . It is also one of the few known planes in the Multiverse where humanity has not flourished. The plane was considered to be "spark-blind" (unaware of planeswalkers or other planes) during the events of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor block . However, following the New Phyrexian Invasion and subsequent opening of Omenpaths leading to the plane, many more visitors from other planes have been finding their way to Lorwyn-Shadowmoor.

The plane of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor contains two distinct planar entities: Lorwyn, the day aspect, and Shadowmoor, the night aspect. The two are kept separate, either by the Great Aurora, as they were during the Age of Oona , or by auroras in the current age. With auroras, the two aspects directly border one another. These borders are mostly set, but they can shift slowly, keeping a balance between day and night. Rarely, entire plots of land can suddenly shift, instantly transforming everything within them. These twin aspects are embodied by the plane's twin worldsoul , Eirdu , and Isilu .
The plane's magic is fed by story. Though this effect is not as strong as the narratively-powered magic of Eldraine , it can have powerful local effects.

Lorwyn is one of two aspects of the plane Lorwyn-Shadowmoor, and the setting of the Lorwyn block . The plane is small, temperate, and believed to be flat. The known portion of the plane, referred to as the Blessed Nation by the elves, is heavily forested and ringed by high mountains , outside of which lays the mysterious Primal Beyond. The world has no oceans or large lakes; all of its water comes from a system of rivers and streams connected by the subterranean Dark Meanders . Lorwyn exists in perpetual midsummer and eternal daytime, though its denizens still operate on a daily cycle. The plane observes dawn, noon, and dusk, with no night, with its day beginning when the sun grazes the eastern horizon and ending as it grazes the western. An abnormal "smeared" moon sometimes appears in the sky.

Shadowmoor, the setting of the Shadowmoor block , is the other facet of the plane Lorwyn-Shadowmoor. Whereas Lorwyn was defined by its greenness, especially its forests, its dark reflection is practically devoid of green. Shadowmoor exists in perpetual night, where the moon travels back and forth, cycling each month between full and new but never disappearing, and the sun never is directly visible. Though the sun appears perpetually eclipsed and is often hidden behind a blanket of cloud, Shadowmoor still observes dawn, dusk, and night, albeit without noon.

Shadowmoor is suffused with wild magic, a magic inherent to the plane that overflows with power and energy. Wild magic is a deep well of power that anyone can draw upon. This power is chaotic and volatile, and can cause catastrophic backlashes that destroy both its caster and the surrounding environment.

During the Age of Oona, the entire plane would shift between Lorwyn and Shadowmoor because of the Great Aurora, a magical convergence orchestrated by the faerie queen herself. After her defeat, the plane of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor is constantly at odds, with massive swaths of land covered by the light of Lorwyn or the darkness of Shadowmoor, their boundaries ebbing and flowing. Sometimes, deaths or births within a particular mass of land might expand or shrink the size of Lorwyn or Shadowmoor. Other times, these boundaries might shift due to the influence of Eirdu's or Isilu's footfalls. And even more frequently, these borders will grow or shrink without rhyme or reason as a way for the plane to naturally correct imbalances in power, influence, or size. By around 4564 AR , these boundaries had grown more stable, resulting in some relatively permanent borders.

When these boundaries shift, everything within them transforms, including creatures and all other living entities. Though there are methods to suppress this change, these are rare, and creatures or other objects that are immune to these changes are even rarer. Where the boundaries of Lorwyn and Shadowmoor abut, you can see beyond one's current aspect and into the other. Native-born creatures on the plane have two forms: a Lorwyn form and a Shadowmoor form. When an aurora occurs, and Lorwyn becomes Shadowmoor or vice versa, all creatures and aspects of the landscape within that area undergo a massive transformation. To cross from Lorwyn to Shadowmoor is known as Eventide, and to cross from Shadowmoor to Lorwyn is Morningtide. Though creatures do not change their species, they are physically and mentally altered. They might also undergo dramatic personality shifts. Overall, denizens of Lorwyn are more communal and orderly, while denizens of Shadowmoor are more individualistic and chaotic.

Memories are not preserved between the auroral boundaries; the natives of one aspect of the plane don't recall their previous lives when crossing into the other aspect, and instead remember having always lived in the current iteration of the plane. Their memories from the originating aspect become murky and muddled, and are reconstructed into distorted remembrances of the current aspect that mirror their experiences from the other. They regain their true memories of their Lorwyn or Shadowmoor self if they recross the threshold. These changes in memory aren't undocumented, however. Many species understand the danger of crossing the threshold and the pain that may accompany it. Even if they desired to know their other self, they would lose the life they knew in the process.

There are, however, a handful of beings in recent memory who retain their memories by way of ritual or circumstance: the former fae queen Oona and her two creations, Maralen and Oko , who were both constituted with her own essence; Ashling , who bonded with a greater elemental ; and Rosheen Meanderer , who was born during a Great Aurora centuries previously. Additionally, all faeries are shielded from the aurora by remnants of Oona's magic, with only their appearance and disposition changing, at most. Non-native beings are not affected by auroras.

Where the boundaries of Lorwyn and Shadowmoor grind against one another, pockets of new environments emerge. These regions are known as eclipsed realms and represent a third state of neither light nor shadow that the plane can take. They range in size from a few square feet to several square miles. The eclipsed realms are strange and otherworldly, even when compared to the rest of the plane. They exist along the borders between aspects, with some eclipsed realms appearing as slivers and others covering massive swaths of land. In eclipsed realms, the sun and moon float high in the sky or are overlaid near the horizon, bathing the area in an eerie, gleaming twilight that never turns to night or brightens into day. These strange places are wrapped in iridescent, colorful fog.

Eclipsed realms are uninhabited but often contain natural features like forests, mountains, and rolling plains. Within these regions, a denizen of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor is not immediately transformed into another aspect of themself. They retain all memories of their time outside the realm and slowly regain any memories of their time spent in the other aspect. However, as they remain in an eclipsed realm, they slowly and permanently transform. Travelers from Lorwyn begin to take on aspects associated with Shadowmoor and vice versa, as the effects of both lands struggle for dominance. Their memories of one aspect try to combine with the memories of the other, and the contradictions between them cannot be fully resolved. These eclipsed creatures lose their desires, emotions, and connection to the world outside, eventually turning into husks who cease movement entirely. When this occurs, they are known as calciform creatures, or simply calciforms .

While the transformations might seem inevitable to the common folk of Lorwyn and Shadowmoor, there was once an ancient relic known as the Crescent of Morningtide, empowered by a great elemental, that could bridge the gap between aspects without changing. In the same way, the people of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor have constructed reliquaries from pieces of the incarnations of day and night. A reliquary allows a person to retain their physical form and memories between aspects, including passing through eclipsed realms. These reliquaries are fashioned from pieces of Eirdu and Isilu. Such items are rare and often sacred, representing the distilled essence of either Lorwyn or Shadowmoor. To resist the Eventide, you must carry a Reliquary of Dawn fashioned from a piece of Eirdu; to resist the Morningtide, you must carry a Reliquary of Twilight fashioned from a piece of Isilu. It is said that possessing both allows you to traverse eclipsed realms unchanged. Reliquaries can take many forms but are commonly designed as lanterns or pendants that light or shade the way. Their form often depends on the piece of the incarnation they are fashioned from. For example, a feather might be turned into a brooch, while a glowing scale could be placed inside glass and turned into a lantern. Elves are known to carry small sunlight elementals within cages of briar as makeshift Reliquaries of Dawn.
The following sets have taken place on Lorwyn-Shadowmoor:
Lorwyn-Shadowmoor block Lorwyn Morningtide Shadowmoor Eventide

Millenia before 4500 AR , Oona , queen and mother of all faeries , used the Great Aurora to grant herself control of the plane by manipulating its celestial cycle. Every three hundred years, the plane would alternate entirely between its two aspects, shifting into states of perpetual Lorwyn or perpetual Shadowmoor. This left its inhabitants ignorant to both the other half of the world and their prior existence, free to be easily controlled and pitted against each other, all while Oona maintained her own memories as a means to exert her command over both halves of the plane. This continued until the cycle was disrupted in 4520 after the Great Mending , an event that healed the entire Multiverse of damage from accumulated time rifts . For the first time in eons, Oona feared she might be affected by the Great Aurora, prompting her to create a vessel that could bear her memories through the plane's approaching transformation. After the first avatar she created— a shapeshifter named Oko who turned his inherited intellect against her— rebelled and fled, she created a duplicate Maralen , a Mornsong elf , and instilled the imposter with a piece of her own soul. Oona envisioned her new creation as a subjugated successor whose sole purpose was to preserve her memories and identity. However, " Maralen " gained sentience just as Oona's first creation had and banded together with others from across Lorwyn to investigate Oona and the effect she was having on the plane.

Once the Great Aurora occurred and transformed the plane into Shadowmoor, Oona was defeated by a coalition consisting of Maralen, an elf named Rhys , a flamekin named Ashling , a kithkin named Brigid , a merrow named Sygg , a treefolk named Colfenor , and his unnamed sapling . Though Oona was defeated and her body was destroyed, her unforgiving consciousness remained, determined to reclaim her seat of power and become whole once more. Following the end of her reign, the plane began to fuse , triggering the start of the Pendulum Year . Maralen took on the mantle of queen of the fae and bound herself to Rhys, granting him immortality in exchange for keeping tireless vigil over her, fearing that a day might come when she'd find herself being corrupted by Oona's power.

Across Shadowmoor, pockets of Lorwyn sprouted up in the darkness. The plane was thrown into turmoil, since any person or place could be transformed in a moment. Entire villages were split in two, and anyone crossing these new borders changed instantly. Farmers were cut off from their farms or forgot their trade entirely; communities were estranged from their neighbors, unable to contact anyone through these new borders. At times, there were even periods of day into night into day, mimicking the day and night cycles of other planes.

Soon, there was a slowing of these transformations. Borders seemed to stabilize and inched forward like gentle tides rather than crashing waves. People began to see two great beings: Eirdu , the incarnation of Lorwyn, and Isilu , the incarnation of Shadowmoor. The twin worldsoul of the plane had emerged again to control the ebb and flow of the plane's auroras. For the next forty years, the plane enjoyed peace maintained by the existence of these two incarnations. Sometimes, startling tales would emerge from a distant village, that their neighbors and homes had been caught between the light and darkness and succumbed to something that was both and neither at the same time. These areas came to be known as eclipsed realms.
Following the Age of Oona, the elves tightened their grip on the plane. Eyeblights were heavily culled, with some boggart communities dwindling to extinction.

The New Phyrexian Invasion (recorded and referred to by some of Lorwyn's races as inneal ionnsaigh ) destroyed the fragile power balance of the plane and forced species to cooperate in ways they had never considered before. In particular, the Lorwyn elves that had once terrorized the denizens of Lorwyn were nearly decimated, their dominion over the plane turned into networks of power for the Phyrexians . The compleated elves used their cruelty and prejudice to great effect, the oil having hardly even changed their behavior toward other species. The elves that remained untainted were pushed back and, in a desperate gamble, allied themselves with the other species of Lorwyn. In doing so, they were finally able to gain ground and make a stand at Lys Alana. The Phyrexians would resort to new tactics, like infecting kithkin and using the thoughtweft to poison their comrades' minds, or sending corrupted faeries to stealthily infect water supplies.

In Shadowmoor, chaos reigned as each species mounted assaults against their invaders in any way they saw fit. Their scattered approach was less effective than the unified front of Lorwyn, but they saw far fewer losses as a result. Only the boggarts and kithkin made courageous stands against the invaders. The boggarts formed the vanguard, riding their cavalry into the enemy lines and gutting them from within. They suffered massive casualties, as they expected. As Halo poured through the Multiverse, it was the isolationist Shadowmoor kithkin that led the last charge to destroy the invaders. Driven by a xenophobia that surpassed anything they'd ever felt toward their fellow planar denizens, they crushed ranks of Phyrexians and trampled them underfoot. Afterward, with their fears of outsiders made manifest, the kithkin holed themselves up in their homes, unwilling to see guests even years after.

The current age of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor is one of tenuous peace. Not all changes are predictable, as villages might be transformed at a moment's notice and their inhabitants made unaware that they once lived a different life. The emergence of the mysterious eclipsed realms threatens to further confuse the people of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor, who are now wary of yet another unknowable change to their world. In the political realm, the empire of the Lorwyn elves has dwindled in power, allowing other species to gain footholds in the world where they were previously denied. Without Oona turning the other species against one another, trade and commerce flourish, each species leveraging their unique talents to achieve newfound prosperity.
Ballyrush - a kithkin clachan known for its stock of springjacks
Bristlebane - considered the most violent doun in Shadowmoor.
The Bubbling Bog - a swampy area often used as a curse by kithkin .
Burrenton - a kithkin clachan known for its smiths and forges Lake Laightle
Cloverdell - a kithkin clachan protected by treefolk
Duinshyle - a kithkin clachan far from Kinsbaile .
Dundoolin - the second largest kithkin clachan , known for its sages who record elemental history.

Eastern Lorwyn - dominated by the Gilt-Leaf Wood . Gilt-Leaf Wood - the beautiful, gold-shimmering forest of the Gilt-Leaf elves , bordered by the Wanderwine River and covering more than half the lands of Lorwyn. Lys Alana - the Gilt-Leaf capital city. Dawn's Light Palace - the last remaining palace of the elves, pinnacle of elvish perfection. It is known as Caer Ulios in Shadowmoor. Glen Elendra - haven of the great Faerie Maralen (and formerly of elusive Oona , queen of Lorwyn's faeries). It lies far south of Lys Alana . Glen Priseil - the seat of the false queen Oura and her band of supporters. A secluded valley boasting a rushing waterfall and an idyllic pond. Oak Fall - where Taercenn Grieve ruled during his lifetime.
Fen Grieve - a river port where the statue of Taercenn Grieve stands.
Frogtosser warren - a group of boggarts so emotionally changeable that the other warrens think them insane.
Funnelwood Forest - a distant wood full of widow spiders and their silk webs.
Goldmeadow - a small kithkin clachan known for its wheat fields and militia training.

The Grave of Nath - After Nath , a cruel elvish hunter, was slain by Rhys , his body was interred in a grove. The grove has gone wild, hosting all manner of deadly, poisonous plants, and legends say Nath's soul still yearns for revenge.
Howltooth Hollow - a cave that secretly imprisoned a barghest .
Longlake Clachan : a clachan located along a small brackish lake, known for its shipbuilding and for producing the best swimmers among all kithkin.

The Merrow Lanes or simply "the Lanes" - Lorwyn's network of riverways, system of rivers and streams, subterranean channels, and even village wells. The Dark Meanders , or the Dark Tributaries - the waterways that run purely underground. The Honeystone River - drunk dry by the treefolk monk Adair River Span . Shelldock Isles - ancient shells used by Lorwyn's denizens as picnic spots before they awoke into kraken during Aurora. The Swiftbend River - a river whose course was changed by Colfenor to save a stand of birch saplings from a flood. The Wanderwine River - the greatest Lane, a low-country river lined with merrow crannogs, flowing from Mount Tanufel in the north and to the tip of the lowlands on the southeastern shore. Crannog Aughn - Sygg 's home crannog
Mornsong - The forest of the eponymous tribe of elves. Arbor Morning - capital of the Mornsong elves.
Mosswort Bridge - a bridge under which a troll was imprisoned.

The Mountain ranges - realm of giants , some wanderlust-stricken flamekin , and hostile greater elementals . There is one northern range and one western coastal range. Amphitheater of Galanda Feudkiller - giant dolmen stones arranged in a bowl shape where conflicts are resolved swiftly and violently. Mount Tanufel - the tallest peak on Lorwyn, sacred birthplace of the flamekin . Ember Fell - a flamekin monastery. The Source of Lanes - the source of the Wanderwine is a small lake a few hundred feet from the summit of Tanufel. Tanufel Crater - the flat top of the peak, the highest point on the plane. Spinerock Knoll - an overgrown, dragon-shaped mountain that housed the dragon Knollspine . The forge-tenders of Burrenton traditionally use pebbles from the Knoll, whose magic gives their fuel consistent heat. Its barren crater in Shadowmoor would later serve as inspiration for dragonfire-obsessed witches . Now returned to its natural state on Lorwyn, the outcropping has become home to flamekin who worship Knollspine and hope to be reborn as dragons themselves.
Mudbutton Warren - a particularly chaotic and loud Boggart warren that appreciates a good party.
The Stand of Tulimeer - an outpost of treefolk and other trees attempting to establish a new forest on a rocky outcropping near flamekin lands.

Squeaking Pie Warren - known for its culinary adventurousness. Boggarts from other warrens often claim Squeaking Pie lineage so they can attend their Footbottom Feasts, which are widely thought to have the tastiest food. The warren's recipes are its most prized possessions, and its boggarts will go to any lengths to find bizarre new recipes and ingredients. The warren is led by Auntie Jowl, who raises the mice that often end up in the warren's famous savory pies.
Stinkdrinker Warren - known for its stockpile of stolen goods and its boggarts' penchant for sneaking past even giants to steal their prizes. Located along the Wanderwine.
Taenskarper - a hilly, forsaken area where the elves and boggarts sometimes wage battles.
Tanfell Plateau - an overhang bordering the Wanderwine River , from which cold winds sweep down, creating whitecaps in the water.

Toetap Mire - A vast wetland with a reputation for absorbing the creatures and plants that perish in its waters, resulting in a liquid with strange properties. Boggart apothecaries seek the swamp's water for use in all manner of potion-making.
Velis Vel - a subterranean crystal cavern associated with Lorwyn's changelings , accessible through the Dark Meanders .

Western Lorwyn - often contrasted with the Gilt-Leaf Wood , the western Lorwyn is the half of the land on the north and west side of the Wanderwine . Dauba Ravine - a ravine separating the west edge of the Porringer Basin and the foothills of the mountains. Spanned by a bridge. The Great Forest - a seemingly endless expanse of stout-trunked oaks and other mighty trees. Murmuring Bosk - a sacred grove of treefolk , far from Kinsbaile , along the Wanderwine River . Wren's Run - a mazelike stretch of forest considered the plane's finest hunting grounds. Groundling Town - a rotting log, fortified by the Sapling of Colfenor 's magic, home of the plane's groundlings . Kinsbaile - the largest kithkin clachan , host of the Festival of Tales . Lies on the north bank of the Wanderwine , not far from the base of Mount Tanufel . The Kinsbaile Dock - the river ferry dock closest to the clachan. The Kinswood - a copse of trees just outside the Kinsbaile gates. Porringer Basin - formerly a heavily wooded broad lowland and home of the ash treefolk known as Porringer Valley. Now flooded, causing an influx of merrow who have set about repurposing the valley into a nursery. Warywind Bough - a secretive meeting place for the faeries of Lorwyn that's secluded behind a waterfall. Many plots and schemes are hatched here. Few who stumble upon Warywind Bough are welcome unless they agree to take part in the faeries' mischief.
Windbrisk Heights - a raptor whose wings were frozen for generations in the shape of a blustery cliff.
Ashenmoor - the black home of cinders .

The Ash Forge - an imposing edifice churning smoke into its surroundings. Within its walls is a forging device designed by Shadowmoor flamekin that produces weapons imbued with the desire to extinguish all life.
Ballynock - a kithkin doun , whose inhabitants like to wear hoods.
Barrenton - a kithkin doun .
Bellowrath - a village of exiled flamekin, where doomsday cults prophesize that the world will end in a billowing cloud of ash from Mount Kulrath's eventual eruption.
Boreal Ridge a cliffside rimekin settlement.

Creakwood Caer Flur - the largest settlement in Shadowmoor. The Eluvian - an enormous tree that elves use as a gathering place. Dawnglove Grove - deep within the Creakwood is a grove of dawnglove , constantly guarded by the most elite of the Shadowmoor elves, irrespective of clan. Grove of the Ashblossoms , Grove of the Aurora Queen or Glade of the Aurora Queen - a peculiar forest of flowering trees that grew from the corpse of Oona's flower, which was buried deep in the Creakwood. A few faeries revere the grove, believing the ashen trees contain a portion of her spirit.
The Dark Meanders - underground rivers connecting to the Wanderbrine.
Druim Calad - the only major aboveground port in Shadowmoor.
Dundaeron - a kithkin doun .

Eastern Shadowmoor Glen Elendra - formerly the haven of Oona ; Maralen makes her home here now. It is glamered to protect it from those in Shadowmoor who would destroy its beauty. It lies far south of Cayr Ulios . Wilt-Leaf Wood - just east of Mistmeadow, across the Wanderbrine . Barrenclay Crossings - a meeting point for the Wilt-Leaf elves. Cayr Ulios - the largest safehold in Wilt-Leaf Wood .
Greasewretch Warren - a boggart warren that is the equivalent of Mudbutton Warren.

Greymeadow - a kithkin doun , whose inhabitants like to wear helmets. First Gate - the inner gate in Greymeadow. Second Gate - the middle gate in Greymeadow. Outer Gate - the outermost gate in Greymeadow.
Isilu's den - A seemingly freestanding dolmen gate that leads to a cave used by Isilu for its hibernation during Lorwyn's phase in the cycle.
The Lanes The Wanderbrine - the big river cutting Shadowmoor in two. The Withervine - a river flowing far from the Wilt-Leaf Wood .
Lochran Safehold - a safehold by the Withervine River, far from the Wilt-Leaf Wood .
Mount Kulrath - the highest peak on Shadowmoor.

Pokeprodder Bog - most creatures would contract a plague from sloshing around these swamps, but the boggarts that call this place home are immune to its properties and have even become poisonous as a result.
Rotbog Warren - one of the calmest and stable warrens in Shadowmoor. Boggarts here have built a massive tower through rudimentary means, though its frequent teetering betrays its slipshod creation.
The Serpent's Maw - a maze of caves containing a river of burning stone.
Thistledown - a kithkin doun

Western Shadowmoor Kinscaer - a kithkin doun south of Mistmeadow . Mistmeadow - a kithkin doun north of Kinscaer The Welk Lodge Raven's Run - a dark and terrifying forest The Weeping Bosk - the place where Colfenor trained Rhys in the use of yew magic.
Wretchgrinder Warren - boggarts deemed too weak to fight in battle are sent here to die. Should a boggart survive the ordeal, it is known as a "wretch" and is sent to die again, but in battle.
Currency on Lorwyn is composed of skeins of precious metal, in denominations of copper, silver, and gold, grouped in size into threads, ropes, and coils.

A rudimentary pictographic Boggart language, created after the New Phyrexian Invasion . Used to document new magical rituals, it was originally etched into bark and stone. Known symbols include "danger," "safety," "resources," and most commonly "adventure awaits."
The language of the elves.
The true tongue of the flamekin is a collection of whispered scrapes and hollow exhalations of brimstone, unreproducible by the other races of the plane.
Merrow, which uses the merfolk's glamer magic as an "emotional flavor". "Paupurfylln" is the Merrow name for the school called Paperfin by other cultures.
A sign language used by the merrow.
The New Phyrexian Invasion is called inneal ionnsaigh , the Scottish Gaelic translation of "metal invasion".
Standing stones are often carved with runic script similar to Pictish .

The indigenous wildlife of the Lorwyn is dominated by eight sapient species : elves , kithkin , merrows , flamekin , boggarts , treefolk , giants , and faeries . Lorwyn is one of the few known places in the multiverse where humans do not occur naturally. In addition, Lorwyn supports a menagerie of animal and supernatural life, including wisents, springjacks , cervins , a semisapient species of mimics known as changelings and the majestic greater elementals . All of them thrive in Lorwyn's temperate environment and unending growing season, preserving the plane's character as an unspoiled natural wilderness.

Each of the nine species (including the Changelings), known as the Tribes , lives in an uneasy state of peace; skirmishes and small battles occur from time to time, but full-scale war is unknown. The Tribes are highly provincial and distrustful of those outside their species; all are wary of the cruel and powerful elves , who function as the plane's de facto rulers.

Lorwyn is a backwater world rarely visited by planeswalkers . Those who know of its existence regard it as an idyllic paradise. Late in Lorwyn's history, the barriers between the Tribes began to break down as individuals from different species came together into new tribes based on common goals ( soldiers , wizards , and so on).

Eternalisks, extremely rare, immortal creatures that dwell high up in the mountains. Any part of them, but particularly their scales, can be used to make potent healing charms that can regrow lost limbs or heal even the most hopeless ailments. Possibly related to basilisks .

Cattails - a puffy river reed.
Deathcap - a poisonous mushroom.
Grass Arrowgrass - a plentiful, sturdy wild grass used by elves for arrow shafts.
Hemlock - a poisonous plant.

Moonglove - a white, foxglove-like flower with pale-blue pistils cultivated by Lorwyn's elves to derive a potent poison called "Moonglow". This poison is deadly even in small amounts, taking down even towering giants . The elves use moonglow aggressively in battle, where it is the source of their fame and feared " deathtouch ". It kills in minutes, spreading bruise-purple marks up the victim's body. In precisely controlled, highly diluted trace amounts, its necrotizing properties can be used to etch or carve living tissue, such as skin or bark. Moonglove is also essential in many other important elf rituals and magic.
Nettlevine - a parasitic plant that the elves can animate to bind around their victims, creating the vinebred - twisted, but powerful and eminently controllable minions.
Nightshade - a poisonous berry

Trees Alder - a water-loving tree. Ash - a tall tree. Birch - a pale tree. Black Poplar - prevalent in the Murmuring Bosk . Mangrove Oak - a large, sturdy tree Rowan - a flowering tree Silverwood pine - a needle-bearing tree from which the Gilt-Leaf fashion sharp arrows. Yew - a poisonous tree. A needle coated in yew poison is enough to send an elf into a short coma, but the vinebred are completely immune to yew toxin.

Some creatures that are dormant in Lorwyn are active in Shadowmoor, while others now hide from sight on the new plane. Ouphes , korrigans , pucas , kelpies , scarecrows , and nightmarish , mythical beings that had slumbered beneath Lorwyn's surface have reemerged in the ambient night. What species have survived the change have been thoroughly altered by the tainted darkness covering Shadowmoor. In particular, the demeanor of each species has taken a turn for the worse. The kithkin have become withdrawn and distrusting of the other inhabitants of the plane and the boggarts are now violent brutes. The flamekin , now called cinders , have lost their passion and become hateful shadows of themselves; giants have lost their intelligence, and rely in their basic instincts; the merrows are spiteful pirates and raiders who lurk in their murky rivers; the treefolk are warped skeletons of bark and branches; and the playful changelings have become the malicious mimics .

The elves , in contrast, were one tribe to experience a more positive difference. They became the last remnant of Lorwyn's older, idyllic environment. Pressed by hostile conditions, the elves were forced to battle for their very existence. Rather than lording over the plane and oppressing the other species to conform to their values of beauty and grace, the ironic reversal in their situation shifted the elves from arrogance to humbled self-preservation.
The only species that remained mostly the same is the fae because they are protected by Oona's magic, and thus have remained mischievous and unpredictable.

Flowers Brambles Cramoisy - "the killing flower", a deadly poisonous bloom. Dawnglove - Shadowmoor's mirror of moonglove. They grow in small patches, glowing pink, purple, and blueish white. Only found in the areas of Shadowmoor untouched by light, dawnglove is considered sacred as the apex of beauty for the Shadowmoor elves and is distilled into a gleaming purple-gold potion called dawnglow. Dawnglow can be used to cure nearly any ailment, including death itself, but its priceless beauty means that Shadowmoor elves rarely consider using even a petal of this precious flower. Living dawnglove will change with the auroras like anything else, but if plucked, it retains its form, making it an incredibly rare and valuable material in Lorwyn. Flax Water lilies

Lorwyn-Shadowmoor is inspired by Celtic folklore. To a lesser degree, it draws inspiration from the mythology of the rest of the British Isles, including Irish, English, Welsh, and Scottish stories, languages, and cultures.
